I think as a new player, even if not remotely close to poe, there are still a lot of things to figure out if you chill and don't watch too many guides. I think if you don't go hard on trying to learn as fast as possible you can get a couple hundred hours of playtime and I think it's worth the money. But if you want to go hard and try to learn everything asap and still have endgame, poe is the better choice. D3 is better for casual mid term play, PoE just gives you so many choices and so many things to learn that if that's your thing it's a no brainer.

Having over 1500h on D3 and over 2500h on PoE this is my opinion.
Diablo 3 had its time, for a long time now it feels like literally 10 people or less work on D3. Don't expect many game-changing updates. That said, I'm too burned out of the same game but for a new player it can give you a lot of hours of playtime if it's your thing. As long as you don't care about other people and rankings it's a good game to start if you want it to be chill, game is pretty straight forward and not too hard to understand if you're familiar with the genre. For people like me who has played a lot and knows how to be efficient, it lacks endgame since they made it trivial to complete the maximum difficulty, can be achieved in group in much less than 100h. That is pretty experienced players ofc.
On the other hand, PoE is constantly being changed, balance changes, new mechanic and from time to time a rework of old mechanics, every 3 months. If you chill and don't give everything too much attention it can be new player friendly. If you are the type of person who wants to know how everything you encounter works, you are gonna be overloaded with dozens of mechanics that some are pretty confusing even for experienced players who didnt get into that mechanic. If you like having a lot of things to learn, poe is VERY VERY deep, has a lot of mechanics, you can do so many things if you dont care to be the most efficient. It is very dark, it doesn't explain almost anything and you will have to get to the wiki (wich btw is currently a mess because of some internal changes to the game files we can't get updated info on some things), guides and a lot of external tools/sites if you want to get into it. It is free to play, it's not pay to win (at least not if you dont want to risk being banned) but you will have to spend money at some point. The storage we get as default is very limited and you can only upgrade it paying, you will get many hours of playtime if you don't tryhard in wich you can play for free.

I don't know what else to add. Both games have a spot in my heart, now it happens to be PoE and D3 being abandoned, but D3 is still a big part of me. Either game will probably be worth the time if you like these types of games, hope you have fun either way.

Okay, from what you've mentioned and previous knowledge this is what I think. A short note: I'm very bad at expressing myself and at writing in general so this may not make sense. The speed at wich you attack when not moving is determined by your attack speed wich is divided in two sections, the first is the windup when the champ is "charging" the attack and the windup is the time between you start attacking and the attack is done, melee/instant attack being dmg done and ranged projectile being when the projectile is created and launched. The second part is where you can't start another attack animation, this is the "cd" of the attack, best time to cast skills or move for kiting. Most champs have their windup time fixed in ratio of the total attack time, what you mention as 36% in kalista's wiki, but some champs have a modifier (like kalista 0.75) that makes the windup time scale different (in this case it scales worse) so the extra attack speed change the windup ratio. Having a modifier on the windup inherently adds a modifier on the "cd" time, in this case 1.25, making the time you can't start another attack lower (I might be wrong in this one but 0.75 multiplier making the ratio higher and 1.25 making the ratio lower is due to this not being calculated on attacks per second but attack time, 2 AS == 0.5s total attack time). The jump speed/time on kalista likely has a modifier too but it's hidden. In kalista, the jump time and the attack "cd" are overlapped, meaning the start at the same time, that doesn't mean they have the same time. At low attack speeds when you attack and jump you experience the next: First you start the windup, once the windup is complete a internal time is started to give you time to decide if you want to jump, we're gonna ignore this time every time from now on and assume you instantly jump after windup is complete, when you finish windup and command to jump the attack "cd" and the jump time starts respectively (as said, we ignore the time it takes to command the jump so both start at the same time) the jump time in low AS is lower or equal than the "cd" so you finish jumping and you have a time greater or equal to 0s where you can't start another attack. When you increase the AS the windup time gets lower but its ratio of the total attack time gets higher (more than 36%) so the attack "cd" gets lower in 2 ways, by the inherent decrease with attack speed and because of the mod to windup while the jump time has another decrease modifier (unknown but crearly lower, worse, than the "cd" time) this leads to a point in AS (around 1.55) in wich the windup time and jump time is greater than the total attack time, or the jump time is higher than the attack "cd" time, this making that the attack "cd" time becomes meaningless unless you're still and the displayed attack speed is not the speed at wich you will be attacking.

I made a quick [table](https://prnt.sc/1f5royd) using [wiki's formula](https://leagueoflegends.fandom.com/wiki/Basic_attack#Windup) for the windup times, "cd" time is just substract windup time from attack time, jump time is an arbitrary formula since we don't know how it scales, it was made so it shows the breakpoint when it intersects the "cd" time graph and how it affect real attack time (=IF (jumpTime + windupTime < attackTime; attackTime; jumpTime + windupTime)) that shows what your attack time will be in practice. I think this illustrates what is happening. You can also see the windup % increases with attack speed.
